name: Transient Myeloproliferative Syndrome

ethnicAssociations: Higher incidence in individuals with Down syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of circulating blast cells in peripheral blood
Clinical features consistent with myeloproliferative disorder in neonate with Down syndrome
Spontaneous resolution of abnormal myeloproliferation within 3 months
Detection of GATA1 gene mutation in blast cells

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of circulating blasts with clinical features in a neonate with Down syndrome plus detection of GATA1 mutation or spontaneous resolution within 3 months
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and genetic; bone marrow biopsy may be supportive but is not always required.

searchTerms: presence of immature blast cells in blood

pathognomonic.symptomName: GATA1 gene mutation in blast cells
searchTerms: GATA1 gene mutation in immature blood cells

common.symptomName: Congestive heart failure secondary to high-output state
searchTerms: heart failure from high blood flow state
congestive heart failure due to increased output
heart failure caused by high-output condition

rare.symptomName: Leukemic transformation to acute megakaryoblastic leukemia
rare.notes: Occurs in approximately 20-30% of cases but rare in neonatal period

searchTerms: kidney failure caused by blood cell blockage
kidney damage due to blood cell clumping

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing circulating blasts
Thrombocytopenia and anemia on complete blood count
imaging: Echocardiogram may reveal pericardial effusion or cardiac dysfunction
other: Spontaneous resolution of symptoms and blastocytosis within 3 months

distinguishingFeatures: Blast cells present in neonates without Down syndrome

redFlags: Rapid progression to acute megakaryoblastic leukemia
Severe respiratory distress or cardiac failure
Persistent or worsening cytopenias beyond neonatal period
references: Roberts I, et al. Transient myeloproliferative disorder in Down syndrome. Blood. 2013.
Alford KA, et al. GATA1 mutations in transient myeloproliferative disorder and acute megakaryoblastic leukemia. Blood. 2011.
